description:
Atomic structure, arrangement and movement; microstructural development and heat treatment; physical properties of ferrous and nonferrous metals, semiconductors, ceramics, polymers and composites; corrosion and mechanical properties.

* Indicates a 3 hour laboratory taken by students on alternate weeks.
preAndCorequisites:
• Complete 1 of:
    • CHEM101 - Fundamentals of Chemistry from Atoms to Materials (1.5)
    • CHEM102 - Chemical Reactivity Fundamentals with Environmental Applications (1.5)
    • CHEM150 - Engineering Chemistry (1.5)
supplementalNotes: • Not open to students with credit in MECH 325.
title: Properties of Engineering Materials
